title: Data, Methods & Credits
text:
Source. U.S. EPA, 2020 National Emissions Inventory (NEI) Data, https://www.epa.gov/air-emissions-inventories/2020-national-emissions-inventory-nei-data. The NEI is EPA’s inventory of air emissions of criteria pollutants, hazardous air pollutants and some greenhouse gases, available for individual facilities and as county totals. This site uses the facility (point-source) data.
Selection. The Houston Health Department selected the point-source facilities in the CHATTER map area that report at least one CHATTER pollutant, and assigned each to a lettered section of its monitor map: 193 facilities in all.
Pollutants. Benzene and 1,3-butadiene (assessed for cancer risk on the CHATTER site), and hexane, toluene, xylenes, styrene, ethylbenzene and cumene (other health risks). The three xylene entries in the NEI (mixed isomers, m-xylene, o-xylene) are added together as “Xylenes”. In the chart, styrene, ethylbenzene and cumene are grouped as “Other”.

title: Data, Methods & Credits
text:
Methods

A facility’s total is the sum of its reported emissions of the CHATTER pollutants listed above, in tons per year. It does not include other NEI pollutants.
Section totals are the sums of the facility totals in that section.
Totals are calculated from the individual pollutant values, so they may differ slightly from rounded totals published elsewhere.
A facility with no reported value for a pollutant is counted as zero for that pollutant.

title: Data, Methods & Credits
text:
Limitations

Emissions are not exposure. Reported emissions do not show how much of a pollutant reaches any neighborhood; that depends on wind, distance, stack height and weather.
Reported point sources only. Traffic, ships, rail, and smaller or unreported sources are not included.
One year. The figures are for 2020, the inventory year used here; emissions change from year to year.
Map sections. Sections are those drawn on the HHD map. Section H, the south-east corner, has facilities but no CHATTER monitor.

The Houston and Harris County Emissions Inventory website was developed by StatAnalytics IDD, LLC with the Houston Health Department (HHD), which compiled the facility list and the monitor map. It is a companion to the Houston and Harris County CHATTER air-monitoring website.

title: Industrial Emissions in East Houston and Harris County
text:
Air monitors measure what is in the air. This site shows where some of it may come from: the 193 industrial facilities in east Houston and Harris County that reported emitting at least one CHATTER air toxic to the U.S. EPA’s National Emissions Inventory (NEI) for 2020. The Houston Health Department compiled the list and placed each facility in one of the lettered sections of its monitor map.
The chart adds up the reported emissions, in tons per year, for each map section. The colours separate the two pollutants assessed for cancer risk (benzene and 1,3-butadiene) from the other pollutants with health risks.


Emissions are not the same as exposure. How much of a facility’s emissions reaches a neighborhood depends on wind, distance, stack height and weather. The inventory also covers only facilities’ reported yearly emissions, not traffic, ships or other sources. Section H, the south-east corner of the map, has facilities but no CHATTER monitor.



The numbers behind the chart: reported emissions by map section and pollutant (tons per year). Other = styrene + ethylbenzene + cumene.
